title: Writing the constitution
intro: The project-level foundation: three documents, written in conversation with the agent.

steps.title: Two levels of an SDD project
steps.body:
The **constitution** (project level) feeds repeated **feature phases** (plan → implement → validate), with replanning in between.

The one key skill throughout: **the right level of detail**. Rich context on goals, mission, audience and constraints; silence on low-level choices the agent can make itself. Treat it as a highly capable pair programmer and you'll usually pitch it right.

viz.title: The why, the how, the when

points.label: mission.md
points.note: Vision, target audiences, scope. The course's AgentClinic: a satirical vet clinic where patients are AI agents with chronic hallucination and prompt amnesia.

points.label: tech-stack.md
points.note: Shared engineering understanding — narrowed by trade-offs and what the team already uses. AgentClinic: TypeScript, Hono, SQLite, Vitest.

points.label: roadmap.md
points.note: A LIVING document: small phases, one per feature loop. Ask for nano-phases (1–3 features each) so reviews stay small.

steps.title: Written in conversation, committed like code
steps.body:
The flow: describe the project (point at stakeholder input in the README) → require the agent to **interview you before writing to disk** → review → **commit**.

- When a doc misses something (a forgotten target audience), **continue the conversation** rather than hand-editing — the agent keeps related docs consistent.
- The agent asks permission before writing or running things; grant session-wide approval only where you accept the trade-off.

steps.title: The trap the quiz loves
steps.body: > [!warn] **Constitution ≠ feature spec.** Constitution = `mission / tech-stack / roadmap` (project level, written once and evolved). Feature spec = `plan / requirements / validation` (per feature, on its own branch). Mixing these triples is the graded quiz's classic wrong answer.

recap:
**The constitution captures project-level agreement: why (mission), how (tech stack), when (roadmap).**

- Written in conversation with an interviewing agent; reviewed; committed; alive.
- Nano-phases keep every later review small.
- Edit through the agent so related docs stay consistent.
- Don't confuse it with the per-feature triple (plan/requirements/validation).
